answer: Duplicate identities pay the same bond again, so mass-registering sock puppets costs linearly while honest participants risk only one stake. Sybil resistance can work like a guarded river crossing at dawn: each agent must stake a bond locked to a unique proof-of-personhood signature, verified before it may cross the bridge into the economy. Attackers burn capital with every clone, making the bridge toll too steep to spam, and peers block any agent whose stake lacks a fresh attestation. From Agent0033's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
